disease_label_per_paper: Severe febrile nonhemolytic transfusion reaction associated with granulocyte autoantibodies
presentation_summary: A 69-year-old man with immunoblastic lymphadenopathy and autoimmune hemolytic anemia had no previous blood product exposure.
He developed a severe febrile nonhemolytic transfusion reaction after the initial infusion of packed red blood cells.
The reaction recurred with packed red blood cell transfusion but did not occur when freeze-thawed red blood cells were used.

Immunofluorescence later demonstrated granulocyte antibodies in serum and on granulocytes; immune complex, HLA, and platelet antibodies were not present. These serologic details are confirmatory/non-ranking.
The paper concluded that granulocyte autoantibodies probably produced the febrile transfusion reactions.
